rv.q: Meanwhile, Horace and his wife Madge (Sally Ann Triplett, very amusing) bring anti-marital comedy, some of it predictable but entertaining nonetheless.

They each have their own page in The Great American Songbook. With some additions to the film’s score, there are 15 numbers and reprises, every one great to listen to, with Stephen Ridley’s orchestra giving full value without overpowering the voices.

It may not be the most substantial of plots in the world, but it is utterly charming in its execution. Not too taxing for the brain and nothing we haven’t seen before, but it is rich with a sweet nostalgia that shines through no matter how familiar you are with the original movie or story.
